Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Only the diagnosis module is supplied; model architecture and sequence-encoder internals are unspecified. Diagnosis reads `item_emb.weight`, obtains per-position sequence representations through `log2feats(sequence)`, and scores positive/negative items with `predict_score(features, items)`. It does not explicitly extract a final user representation: margin checks use features at all valid sequence positions.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the compatibility view (named `model` in this implementation), metadata, review data, and training histories. Reviews and histories are not used by these probes.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` examines up to ten batches of `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`. Sequence inputs are converted to NumPy; positive and negative tensors are placed on the selected device. Scoring runs without gradients after calling `eval()`. With a compatibility wrapper, that call must reach the actual `view.model` module.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 non-padding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal pairwise cosine similarity, and maps it to `[0,1]`. Higher values indicate greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 means average cosine similarity near zero.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits at positions where the positive ID is nonzero. Higher values indicate stronger sampled-pair separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction with negative margin; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction with margin below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in weak-margin and incorrect-ranking cases.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, gradient analysis, or SVD is performed. Random embedding subsampling estimates alignment; loader-supplied negatives test pairwise ranking.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The result contains `metrics` and corresponding `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`.

These training-batch probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, temporal sensitivity, or user traits. Margins depend on logit scale and negative sampling. Categories are unavailable in this benchmark, so category lists should be empty. Empty valid-position samples produce zero-valued margin metrics, which must not be interpreted as evidence of health.

Sampled HR@10 can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation, even in expectation; repeated sampling reduces variance but does not remove this bias. With one held-out positive, Recall@10 equals HR@10. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish the inconsistency; [RecSys 2025 research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398) evaluates sampling reliability through model separability, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and recovery of ground-truth model rankings. Full-catalog evaluation itself remains limited by incomplete relevance observations.

For this task, a practical diagnostic design is to retain pinned validation HR@10 as the selection objective and compare auxiliary uniform, popularity-matched, and hard-negative rankings on identical users. Stratify results by category, training-item popularity, and history length; measure whether probe improvements track validation improvements across checkpoints. These are proposed checks, not established predictors. [2024 rank-estimation research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) supports correcting sampling-induced rank bias, but does not establish that raw margins or hard-negative performance predict this benchmark. Model-selected hard negatives also change as the model changes, complicating comparisons.

Estimate uncertainty by resampling users within each category, keeping model comparisons paired, then averaging the four category means equally. Report confidence intervals for HR@10 differences; these capture user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models, not candidate-sampling bias or training variability. For the twenty feedback users, compare unseen-item full-catalog top-10 overlap, rank stability, and popularity concentration. Without held-out relevance labels, those checks measure agreement and behavior, not recommendation accuracy; five users per category provide exploratory evidence only.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Only the diagnosis module is supplied; model architecture and sequence-encoder internals are unspecified. Diagnosis reads `item_emb.weight`, obtains per-position sequence representations through `log2feats(sequence)`, and scores positive/negative items with `predict_score(features, items)`. It does not explicitly extract a final user representation: margin checks use features at all valid sequence positions.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the compatibility view (named `model` in this implementation), metadata, review data, and training histories. Reviews and histories are not used by these probes.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` examines up to ten batches of `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`. Sequence inputs are converted to NumPy; positive and negative tensors are placed on the selected device. Scoring runs without gradients after calling `eval()`. With a compatibility wrapper, that call must reach the actual `view.model` module.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 non-padding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal pairwise cosine similarity, and maps it to `[0,1]`. Higher values indicate greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 means average cosine similarity near zero.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits at positions where the positive ID is nonzero. Higher values indicate stronger sampled-pair separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction with negative margin; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction with margin below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in weak-margin and incorrect-ranking cases.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, gradient analysis, or SVD is performed. Random embedding subsampling estimates alignment; loader-supplied negatives test pairwise ranking.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The result contains `metrics` and corresponding `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`.

These training-batch probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, temporal sensitivity, or user traits. Margins depend on logit scale and negative sampling. Categories are unavailable in this benchmark, so category lists should be empty. Empty valid-position samples produce zero-valued margin metrics, which must not be interpreted as evidence of health.
